record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: Theorem 5.7 states that when q is even, a pseudo-oval O(n, n, q) is classical if and only if it is 2-transitive. Can the same conclusion for odd q be proved without using the classification of finite simple groups?

evidence.quote: 6. Prove, without using the classification of finite simple groups, that Theorem 5.7 also holds for q odd.
Theorem 5.7. The pseudo-oval O(n, n, q), q even, is classical if and only if O(n, n, q) is 2-transitive.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let q be an odd prime power and n a positive integer. A pseudo-oval O(n,n,q) in PG(3n-1,q) is a family of q^n+1 pairwise disjoint (n-1)-dimensional subspaces of PG(3n-1,q) such that any three of them generate the whole space PG(3n-1,q). A pseudo-oval is called classical if it arises (via field reduction) from a conic in PG(2,q^n); equivalently, it is the set of (n-1)-spaces obtained from the points of a conic over GF(q^n) under the natural GF(q)-linear representation. The pseudo-oval is said to be 2-transitive if its stabiliser in the collineation group of PG(3n-1,q) acts 2-transitively on its q^n+1 elements.

Prove, without invoking the classification of finite simple groups, that for q odd a pseudo-oval O(n,n,q) is classical if and only if it is 2-transitive.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published proof of the odd-q case of this characterisation of classical pseudo-ovals that avoids the classification of finite simple groups. The result appears to remain a posed open problem; no clear resolution was located.
